To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

L27 domain-mediated assembly is a general mechanism for organizing scaffold proteins into tetrameric complexes and that the C-terminal helices of the L27 domains are specificity determinants for each L27 domains in choosing its binding partners.
L27 domain-mediated heteromeric complexes have a common tetrameric assembly mode but different specificity determinants.

the tetrameric L7/L27 domain assembly mode is a general feature of all L27 domain complexes, and that the specificity of L27 domain interactions is determined by the C-terminal alpha helix of the L27 domains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis of LIM and L27 domain interactions.
the structural basis of LIM domain-mediated protein-proprotein interactions.
the structural basis of L7/L27 domain-mediated protein interactions and protein assemblies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
L27 domain complexes are tetramers composed of two heterodimers.
the L27 domain-mediated heterodimeric assembly is a tetrameric complex with a central four-helix bundle, which is formed by the interaction of two heterodimers.

the L27 domain-mediated heteromeric complex formation is a general mode of L27 domain-mediated supramolecular assembly and that each L27 domain complex adopts a tetrameric conformation composed of two units each of heterodimer, with each L27 domain forming a distinct central four-helix bundle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the L27 domain-mediated tetrameric complex assembly is highly versatile in terms of its structural and biochemical features.

the L27 domain-mediated heteromeric complex formation is a general mode for L27 domain scaffold proteins to assemble into supramolecular complexes and that the L27 domains of each scaffold protein have evolved to be specific for their cognate binding partners.
the tetrameric assembly mode of cognate pairs of the L27 domains is conserved, while the specificities for L27 domain interactions are determined by the C-terminal alpha helices of each L27 domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a tetramer is the minimal unit for an L27 domain complex.
L27 domain-mediated assembly is highly specific and is mediated by the formation of a tetrameric complex.
the L27 domain is an extremely versatile protein-protein interaction module.
